the development of transgenic plant feedstocks that produce CWD enzymes to improve bioethanol production.
the use of plant biotechnology to improve lignocellulose conversion efficiency.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CWD enzyme expression in transgenic plant is a promising approach for biofuel production, but it is a long way from commercialization.
transgenic plant production of CWD enzymes is possible but the yield of the enzyme is low.
the production of transgenic plant produced hydrolytic enzymes has the potential to reduce the cost of biofuels production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of insect gut derived CWD enzymes in plants is possible and that this technology has great potential for the biofuels industry.
the use of insect gut derived genes is a viable strategy for improving plant feedstock production of CWD enzymes.
CWD genes can be deployed into transgenic plants, but the results are not always predictable or desirable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insect derived CWD genes are more efficient in transgenic grasses than fungal or bacterial genes.
insect gut derived CWD enzymes are a rich and underexploited resource for biofuels.
insect derived CWD enzymes are more likely than bacterial or fungal enzymes to be expressed in transgenic plants without negative pleiotropic side effects.
